subject: Urgent: AuroraLink latency + 5xx spike (US-East-3) — request for exec bridge
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@auroralink.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Michelle Lopez <m.lopez@auroralink.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T08:17:00-04:00
Subject: Urgent: High latency and 5xx from US-East-3 since 08:00 ET

Priyom —

We started seeing elevated p99 latency (~4.2s -> 12s) and a spike in 5xx across our inference calls routed to US-East-3 starting ~08:00 ET this morning. Throughput has dropped ~35% as clients are retrying. Impact: payments processing (sync) and a subset of low-latency recommendations are failing.

Attached is a short snippet from our client logs (auroralink_error_snippet.log). Our contracts reference a 99.9% availability SLA; this is customer-impacting. Can you confirm:
- If this is a Redwood platform issue or something on our end?
- Immediate mitigation plan and ETA to normalize?
- Whether executive support / credits will be considered?

We’re available on a quick bridge; recommend bringing your SREs and routing ops.

— Samir
Director of Platform, AuroraLink

(Attachment: auroralink_error_snippet.log)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@auroralink.com>
Cc: Michelle Lopez <m.lopez@auroralink.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T08:28:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: High latency and 5xx from US-East-3 since 08:00 ET

Samir — thanks for the heads-up and the log.

Short answer: we see a platform-side degradation in US-East-3 and have SRE on it now. Immediate steps we are taking (I’ll join a bridge in 10):
- Rishi and team are validating AZ3 network fabric and backend queue backpressure.
- We will initiate targeted traffic steering to US-West-2 for affected routes (read-heavy recommendations first) to reduce error exposure.
- If steering is insufficient within 25 minutes we’ll begin rolling failover for AuroraLink’s pinned model slices to US-West-2.
- Enabling a quantized fallback model variant for lower-memory paths to reduce backend CPU/GPU contention.

I’ve attached the current runbook (runbook_v2.pdf) and a proposed traffic-shift graphic. I’m proposing an exec bridge at 09:00 ET to align on customer comms and escalation path — please confirm if that works for your team.

Priyom
Senior AM, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: runbook_v2.pdf, traffic-shift-plan.png)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir.shah@auroralink.com>, Michelle Lopez <m.lopez@auroralink.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T08:36:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: High latency and 5xx from US-East-3 since 08:00 ET

On Fri, Oct 22, 2026 at 08:28 AM Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com> wrote:
> Samir — thanks for the heads-up and the log.

We have SRE telemetry showing repeated network fabric flaps within AZ3 starting at ~07:52 ET which caused a surge of connection resets and queue pile-up on the frontend routers. The router-level backpressure then caused downstream executor queues to back up leading to elevated latencies and a small increase in 5xx from overloaded workers.

Immediate technical actions executed 08:30 ET:
- Isolated the fabric-adjacent hosts and rebalanced router shards.
- Applied transient throttling on top noisy tenants in US-East-3 (we’ve identified three tenants with burst patterns).
- Flipped routing policy for AuroraLink routes to latency_preferred so that the controller will prefer lower-p99 nodes in other regions (US-West-2) for new requests.
- Started progressive drain of a subset of AZ3 worker pools (graceful connection termination, KV cache snapshotting).

Next steps (in-flight):
- Complete traffic steering cutover for recommendation endpoints (expected within 20m).
- If error rate > 1.5% after full shift, trigger full model slice failover for pinned customers and enable quantized fallback.

I’ll post updated metrics and the runbook patch to the Incident Drive link.

— Rishi
Head of SRE, Redwood Inference

(Technical note: we are not seeing persistent host-image corruption; this appears to be network-induced amplification.)

From: Michelle Lopez <m.lopez@auroralink.com>

Thanks — we appreciate the rapid response. Helpful context: impacted endpoints are:
- POST /v1/predict/recs (most critical)
- POST /v1/predict/paymentsync (intermittent failures)

We can join the 09:00 ET bridge. Also, procurement is already asking about SLA credits if this extends past 2 hours. Please include your legal/finance contact on the bridge if possible.

— Michelle
VP Product, AuroraLink

Subject: Exec bridge now live — AuroraLink incident (US-East-3)

Bridge: REDWOOD-INCIDENT-8421 (dial-in + zoom) — joining now. Agenda: quick impact summary, mitigation status, customer comms, credit/contract ask, RCA timeline.

Participants I’ve pulled into the bridge: Rishi (SRE), Hannah (Regional Ops), Laura (Customer Success), Jonas (Head of Platform Eng) — Jonas is standing by for exec-level decisions and credit approvals.

Current status:
- Traffic steering to US-West-2 is at ~65% for recommendation endpoints; p99 for AuroraLink calls trending down to ~2.1s (from 12s).
- Error rate for affected endpoints dropped from 3.8% to 0.9% post-steer.
- We have not yet completed full slice failover; will do so if error rates rebound.

Ask for AuroraLink: confirm if you want us to proceed with a full model-slice failover now (expected 12–15m) or continue gradual steering and observe for another 20m.

I’ll record decisions and post minutes to the Drive.

— Priyom
Senior AM, Redwood Inference
